items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm TP4 with `indexer_decode_cp`, the NVFP4 indexer's context-parallel decode scorer (`ops/index_cp`, from #64111) takes exactly 4 rows per request (DSpark 3). With DSpark 7 (8 rows per request) the gate `query_len != CP_QUERY_LEN` turns CP off without a log line, and every rank scores its index head over the whole context. This PR scores a request of k x 4 rows as k 4-row CP requests on the host, so DSpark 7 keeps the CP path. The kernel does not change.

items.title: [Perf][DSA] Share the prefill indexer's logits schedule across layers on SM100
items.author: Juntian777
items.summary: On SM100, the sparse indexer's prefill builds DeepGEMM's per-SM schedule once per prefill chunk and passes it to in every indexer layer that scores the chunk. Without a schedule, DeepGEMM runs its unbalanced kernel variant, which is slow when rows' KV ranges d…
items.body:
## Overview

On SM100, the sparse indexer's prefill builds DeepGEMM's per-SM `mqa_logits` schedule once per prefill chunk and passes it to `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` in every indexer layer that scores the chunk. Without a schedule, DeepGEMM runs its unbalanced kernel variant, which is slow when rows' KV ranges differ a lot, as in prefix-cache hits on long contexts. The MX weight cast also runs once per layer instead of once per chunk.

items.author: xulunfan
items.summary: On SM120/SM121 the DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate indexer cannot start. SM120 passes the indexer's check, so the candidate path is selected, but DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits kernel requires SM100, so is false and raises before the server reaches readiness.
items.body:
Prerequisite for #47210 (SM120/SM121 dense FP8 native block32 DeepGEMM): without this change DeepSeek-V4.1 does not reach readiness on SM12x with either GEMM backend. The two PRs have zero file overlap and no code dependency in either direction.

## Motivation

On SM120/SM121 the DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate indexer cannot start. SM120 passes the
indexer's `capability[0] >= 10` check, so the candidate path is selected, but
DeepGEMM's paged **sparse** MQA logits kernel requires SM100, so
`DEEPGEMM_PAGED_SPARSE_MQA_LOGITS` is false and `make_candidate_indexer` raises
before the server reaches readine

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1's decoder-side SWA bounded replay pads its sub-batch to the replay CUDA graph size (the largest DP rank's under DP), but the replay forward context passes `is_padding` only under PCP. The padding rows go through expert routing; with garbage hidden states they all pick expert 0 (top-k `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`). This PR marks them as padding so the routers and MegaMoE skip them, as they already do for the outer batch.

## Claims

- Replay-graph padding rows no longer reach MoE experts (DP, no PCP).
- No change to eager replay batches (no padding) or to PCP.

items.body:
NVFP4_PLUS keeps the E2M1 values of NVFP4 but stores one UE5M3 block scale per 32 values and has no FP32 per-tensor scale. The SM107 block-scaled MMA (kind::mxf4nvf4) reads UE5M3 scales directly, and UE5M3 spans 2^-17 to 114688, so activation blocks need no global normalization.

## Motivation

`SGLANG_HIP_DSV41_INDEX_K_PAGE8` stores the ratio-1 index-K pool in AITER's row-group page-8 order. The page size and shapes match page-64; only the bytes differ, so PD peers must agree (the pool's own comment says so). Nothing enforces this today:

- `pd_kv_layout()` covers only the main and compressed KV layouts.
- The transfer compares item lengths, which are the same in both layouts.

items.title: [Feat] openai: Also return chat reasoning text as `reasoning`
items.author: prashant182
items.summary: vLLM's chat completions return the reasoning text as and ( in ), and vLLM no longer sends in responses (vllm-project/vllm#50624 documents that removal as a breaking client change). SGLang returns the same text only as.
items.body:
## Motivation

vLLM's chat completions return the reasoning text as `message.reasoning` and `delta.reasoning` (`ChatMessage.reasoning` in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`), and vLLM no longer sends `reasoning_content` in responses (vllm-project/vllm#50624 documents that removal as a breaking client change). items.title: [RFC]: Large-page KV cache allocator: one KV cache group per spec
items.author: ivanium
items.summary: Proposes replacing vLLM's uniform page-size constraint with a large-page allocator where each KV cache group owns its own large pages, simplifying hybrid model support.
items.body:
**Status:** draft · **Implementation:** two stacked PRs to follow (PR1 opt-in, PR2 large pages only) · **Related:** [#62100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62100) (pluggable KV cache planning)

## TL;DR

vLLM requires every KV cache group to have the same page size in bytes. For hybrid models, this one rule is the source of most of the grouping complexity in core: layer-count grouping, page padding, raised block sizes, `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`, and a second hash granularity (`hash_block_size`). Each new hybrid model, drafter or cache precision tends to need another special case.
discussion:
On 1. I think it should only be hybrid models, no? Or maybe just make it based on number of groups even.

In general on performance, I was first worried that we’d be less flexible with optimisation, but maybe this is not actually the case.

items.author: zhewenl

An eager SimpleCPUOffload store pins its GPU blocks until every worker has copied them, and nothing bounds how many stores are pending. items.body:

## Overview

The packed KV planner caps state buckets (sliding window, circular buffer, mamba) at the widest paged group. That can leave many narrow groups, each reserving its own blocks per request. This PR picks the block width that reserves the fewest bytes per max-length request. The current width is always a candidate, so the new grouping never reserves more per max-length request than the old one.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

When a P/D decode instance gets a burst of requests, each one usually starts with an async KV load. items.body:
## Overview

For asymmetric fp16 W4A16 layers on gfx1151 (Strix Halo), `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` now trades a little weight memory for faster prefill. At load time, each per-group scale and zero-point is packed into one int32 "carrier". Before, it did a scale load, a packed zero-point gather, and a subtract-then-multiply. With the cheaper dequant, asymmetric layers take the packed path from M > 192 (M > 128 when N ≥ 4K) instead of M > 256.

## Description

This PR adds `get_env_flag()` to `tensorrt_llm/_utils.py`. It reads an on/off environment variable the same way everywhere:

- Unset or blank returns the caller's default.
- `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` return True, and `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` return False, in any case and with surrounding whitespace ignored.
- Any other value raises a `ValueError` that names the variable.

## Overview

This lets `method="dspark"` use `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#59973), which so far was limited to EAGLE and MTP. Use `git merge --no-commit --no-ff`, log the before/after diff summary, and add incoming changed paths to the validated mandatory-test list. items.title: [Mooncake] Route KV transfers through a backend interface
items.author: CAICAIIs
items.summary: This PR puts that role behind an interface and wraps the classic engine in an adapter, and the connector stops touching. Behaviour is unchanged: same status text, same per-request failure fan-out, no new configuration key, no wire change.
items.body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeConnectorWorker` creates `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`, asks it for its RPC port, registers KV memory with it, and runs both transfer directions against it, so the connector is bound to one engine implementation.

This PR puts that role behind an interface and wraps the classic engine in an adapter, and the connector stops touching `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`. Behaviour is unchanged: same status text, same per-request failure fan-out, no new configuration key, no wire change.

What the interface covers:

- `register_regions` / `unregister_regions`: pin and release

items.author: cs-fisha

Streaming `InternlmDetector` dropped every tool call after the first when `<|action_start|>` arrived in its own chunk. The full marker is `<|action_start|> <|plugin|>`, and those are separate added tokens, so a token-at-a-time stream splits them.

items.author: amd-dlimpus
items.summary: MiniMax-M3.1 on MI355X (gfx950) can decode from an MXFP4 KV and index cache using the native instructions, which take E8M0 per-32 scales. That's 204 B per token and layer, against 216 B for NVFP4. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Adds `kv_cache_dtype="mxfp4"` for a non-MLA KV cache: E2M1 data with one E8M0 scale per 32 elements (OCP MX), stored as `uint8`.

- `CacheDType` gains `"mxfp4"`, and `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE` maps it to `torch.uint8`.
- `KVQuantMode.MXFP4 = 15`, returned by `get_kv_quant_mode("mxfp4")`, with an `is_mxfp4` property. It is its own mode, not `CUSTOM`, so backends can key on it like `NVFP4`.
- `mxfp4_kv_cache_full_dim(head_size)` gives the packed bytes per head: `head_size / 2 + head_size / 32`, which is 68 for 128. Unlike `nvfp4_kv_cache_full_dim` (72 for 128), there is no global sc

MoE loaders record the padding they narrow away instead of writing it, and the padding is filled right before post-load processing, on every load (0, or 1 for floating-point scales). items.author: akhilg-nv
items.summary: Fixes an IndexError in KVLayerRouter.from_layer_maps when called with empty layer maps, allowing tests to build a router with no token KV sub-pools.
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

A KV pool's `KVLayerRouter` maps each model layer to the sub-pool view that stores its KV. `from_layer_maps` builds
it from one entry per token-KV sub-pool (name, view, layer-to-index map), and parts other than token KV, such as a
request's recurrent state, are bound to it afterwards with `bind_part`. `from_layer_maps` now defaults `owner` (the
sub-pool whose write ids are the request's token ids) to `layer_maps[0][0]`, so an empty `layer_maps` raises
`IndexError: tuple index out of range` (`router.py`, line 180) instead of building a router with no token KV.

The test reserved data_parallel_rpc_port with get_open_port(), which binds port 0 and releases it. launch_core_engines then creates the coordination TCPStore on a kernel-assigned port before binding the handshake socket to the reserved port, so the kernel can hand the freed port to the store and the bind fails with "Address already in use" (seen in the mp and elastic-ep cases).

Use port 0 so the handshake socket picks a free port at bind time.

# RFC: Packed KV block stride (one slot holds all groups' pages)

## Summary

vLLM prices every shared block id at `max_g(per_group_bytes)` and gives each KV
cache group its own id per position. For hybrid models whose groups share one
block index space (equal `block_size`, every group consumes a block per
position) with no sliding-window, no indexer-role cache, and no per-group
alignment, this wastes `max/mean` of the budget. Packing the stride to
`sum_g(per_group_bytes)` makes one id hold every group's page for a position,
recovering that ratio.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Native gfx950 sparse decode for mxfp4_mla rows (on #64121)
items.author: amd-dlimpus
items.summary: Adds a native gfx950 sparse decode kernel for mxfp4 MLA that reads packed rows via scaled MFMA, eliminating costly bf16 unpacking and cutting per-call latency from ~140µs to expected significant improvement.
items.body:
## Overview

At TP2 with more than 4 decode rows, the MonoKernel steps aside and GLM-5.3-Flash runs the regular sparse MLA decode. With the `mxfp4_mla` KV cache (#64121), that decode is the bf16 split-K kernel, which unpacks every selected row to bf16 before the dot products. In a C64 trace it takes 140.1 µs per call against 23.5 µs for the FP8 kernel. Over 11 calls per step that is 1541 µs against 259 µs, and the step goes from 23.50 ms (FP8 KV) to 24.98 ms. This PR adds a gfx950 decode that reads the packed rows on the scaled MFMA instead, with no bf16 or FP8 copy of the cache.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: sets every padded row of a 2D buffer (rows ) to a fill value with one Triton launch. The grid is one program per row, and a program whose row is live exits immediately.
items.body:
## Motivation

`_fill_padded_rows` (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fill_padded_rows.py`) sets every padded row of a 2D buffer (rows `>= num_token_non_padded`) to a fill value with one Triton launch. The grid is one program per row, and a program whose row is live exits immediately. For a large buffer of narrow rows whose padding is a short suffix, the launch is therefore dominated by programs that do nothing, and its cost scales with the buffer rather than with the tail.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Optimizes logprob column flattening in the Rust server by skipping empty rows instead of iterating every batch row per family.
items.body:
## Motivation

In Rust frontend mode, `RustServer.push_generation` runs on the scheduler thread every step, with the GIL held, and flattens the batch's logprob columns into the frame the embedded Rust server decodes. Its per-family filter tested whether a column had any entries. But the output streamer gives every request in a batch with any logprob request a cell in all twelve logprob columns, most of them empty, so the filter never skipped a family: every pair family visited every row of the batch, one bound-method call per row, and filled its value buffer with a per-element `array.extend`.

A prefill over `[s, e)` can only use columns `(s - 1) // B` to `(e - 1) // B`, yet it needs a fixed set of slots: initial state, running state, internal checkpoint, speculative-decode slots. A prefill spanning fewer than about two Mamba blocks does not get enough columns, and the roles collide:

| Columns | Result | Current workaround |
| --- | --- | --- |
| checkpoint column = initial-s

items.author: world-executed
items.summary: Rejects logprobs/prompt_logprobs counts exceeding model vocab size at request validation, preventing worker crashes in torch.topk.

Fixes the validation gap reported in #64291: requests with `logprobs` / `prompt_logprobs` counts larger than the model's vocab size passed `SamplingParams._validate_logprobs()` when `max_logprobs` (default 20) exceeded the vocab size, then crashed the worker at `torch.topk` with `RuntimeError: selected index k out of range` instead of being rejected with a 4xx at request validation. items.title: [Perf] [NPU] allocator: Avoid device synchronization in alloc_extend
items.author: lengthXheight
items.summary: Avoids device synchronization in NPU's alloc_extend by computing page counts from host-side CPU tensors instead of reading back device scalars, reducing latency on the scheduler's allocation path.
items.body:
## Motivation

NPU `alloc_extend` reads the device-computed page count back to the host before it can check capacity and submit the allocation kernel. When `num_new_pages` is omitted, this puts a device synchronization on the scheduler's allocation path:

1. Compute `sum(ceil(seq_len / page_size) - ceil(prefix_len / page_size))` on NPU — six small kernels per allocation.
2. Call `.item()` on that device scalar — the host waits for the scalar and any preceding work on the stream.
3. Check capacity, select the allocation kernel, and update the free-page list using the returned count.

## What does this PR do?

can ever admit it. Because non-chunked scheduling stops at the queue head,

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] DSv4 router: compute sqrt(softplus) with log1p
items.author: FeSens
items.summary: Fixes numerical precision in DeepSeek-V4 router's sqrt(softplus) by using log1p(exp(x)), eliminating incorrect zero routing weights for negative logits.
items.body:
## Overview

The DeepSeek-V4 `sqrtsoftplus` routers compute softplus(x) as log(1 + exp(x)) in fp32. For x below about -16.64, 1 + exp(x) rounds to 1, so the expert's score is exactly 0. Up to about x = -10 the score is off by more than 1e-3 relative (77% at x = -16.6 in the CUDA kernels). This PR computes log1p(exp(x)) instead, in the Triton `dsv4_topk` kernel and in the CUDA `topk_softplus_sqrt` kernels. It makes the same change in the GB300 CuTe DSL MoE front, which must match `dsv4_topk` bit for bit. Related: #49927.

## Claims

- Max relative error of sqrt(softplus(x)) for x in [-30, -5]

items.title: [Fix] pp: Wait on the forward event when skipping output comm
items.author: Robin930
items.summary: (#26148) lets the last PP rank skip the output send/recv for a batch that holds a single non-final chunked-prefill request. That output is a placeholder nobody reads.
items.body:
## Motivation

`SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM` (#26148) lets the last PP rank skip the output send/recv for a batch that holds a single non-final chunked-prefill request. That output is a placeholder nobody reads. Under PD prefill with chunked prefill, enabling the flag currently corrupts the KV cache that is transferred to decode.

**Root cause.** On the last PP rank, `q_event` marks the end of the batch's forward. The output send is the only place the scheduler stream waits on it: `_pp_send_dict_to_next_stage(..., ready_event=q_event)` calls `current_stream().wait_event(q_event)`.

items.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 compute their fp32 router logits on gfx950 with
`_rocm_fp32_router_gemm_kernel` at up to 32 tokens, once per MoE layer per step
(40 times per decode step on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). The fp32 router weight is
384 x 5120 (7.9 MB per layer). The model streams 40 of them per step, so in
decode every call reads its weights from HBM, not from MALL.

The kernel ran with `num_stages=1`. Each program walks K in dependent
iterations, so at 16 tokens the call reaches about 1 TB/s on the weights.
This retunes the launch table for 256 < num_experts <= 512 with a second
pipeline

items.author: andrewzyxing
items.summary: String-stop matching can miss a valid generated spelling when its tokenization is longer than the stop's canonical encoding. For example, Qwen3 encodes as, while decodes to the same.

## Motivation

String-stop matching can miss a valid generated spelling when its tokenization is longer than the stop's canonical encoding. For example, Qwen3 encodes `AAA` as `[50107]`, while `[32,32,32]` decodes to the same `AAA`. With one accepted token per iteration, a canonical count of 1 plus the existing one-token margin searches only the last 2 tokens and never sees the complete stop.

This was observed with a short STANDALONE request: repeated token 32 output stopped correctly for `AA`, but `AAA` reached its length limit. The affected integration source matched public `5cbf949839b1fc7

items.title: [Feat] radix-cache: Bundle SWA KV windows with Mamba checkpoints
items.author: vineelbhat
items.summary: In a unified radix tree with SWA and Mamba components, a cached prefix resumes from a Mamba checkpoint and only needs the SWA KV in the window before it. But the two components evict independently, so SWA eviction can drop a checkpoint's window and make the ch…
items.body:
## Motivation

In a unified radix tree with SWA and Mamba components, a cached prefix resumes from a Mamba checkpoint and only needs the SWA KV in the window before it. But the two components evict independently, so SWA eviction can drop a checkpoint's window and make the checkpoint unusable, while SWA KV that no checkpoint needs stays cached.

This PR adds an opt-in `CacheInitParams.swa_checkpoint_windows` policy that only keeps SWA KV in the window before each cached Mamba checkpoint, and evicts each window with its checkpoint. #47058 builds on it to size DFlash draft KV by Mamba checkpoints

items.title: [KV Offload] Add an external evictor to bound the FS tier's root_dir ( #64239 )
items.author: harsHdokyc
items.summary: The filesystem (FS) KV offload tier has no size limit: every stored block stays on disk forever, so grows until the disk or shared volume fills up. This PR adds a small standalone evictor that keeps under a byte budget, for a single engine or many engines shar…
items.body:
## Overview

The filesystem (FS) KV offload tier has no size limit: every stored block stays on disk forever, so `root_dir` grows until the disk or shared volume fills up. This PR adds a small standalone evictor that keeps `root_dir` under a byte budget, for a single engine or many engines sharing one directory.

Refs RFC #64237, which asks for a cluster-wide quota and coherent eviction for an FS tier shared by many engines. This PR is the smallest useful piece of that: a working size bound with no engine changes.

**Not a duplicate:** #52784 (an in-engine capacity bound) was closed unmerged,

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] MonoKernel: pad a narrow step's inputs once, not every layer (on #61662)
items.author: amd-dlimpus
items.summary: Pads narrow decode-step inputs once instead of per-layer for ROCm MonoKernel, cutting median ITL ~5% by eliminating 164 redundant device copies per step.
items.body:
## Overview

When a decode step has fewer tokens than the MonoKernel's width (one request on width 2, three on width 4), the runtime copied the four mHC inputs into padding buffers before each of the 41 kernel layers. This PR pads once, at the first kernel layer, and chains each layer's padded outputs straight into the next. At concurrency 1 it cuts median ITL by about 5%, and it doesn't change the kernels at all.

**Stacked on #61662**, which has not landed, so the diff against main includes it. This PR's own change is the last commit, `269796ffc2` (+73 / −6: `runtime/layers.py` plus tests).

therefore keeps up to num_experts chunks active per slice and
degenerates to O(n^2) per key. Nothing waits

Add TransformerConfig.cross_entropy_mxfp8_grad (default off). items.title: [None][fix] Give the standalone DSpark drafter its context on KV-cache prefix hits
items.author: zheyuf
items.summary: With KV-cache block reuse on (the default), a standalone DSpark drafter loses its context on every prefix-cache hit. This PR gives it that context back.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

With KV-cache block reuse on (the default), a standalone DSpark drafter loses its context on every prefix-cache hit. This PR gives it that context back.

Why: the drafter builds its context K/V from target hidden states. A cache hit skips the target forward over the reused prefix, and the draft KV pool is not shared with the target's prefix cache. So a cache-hit request drafts from only the uncached tail of its prompt. DSpark also had no `context_recompute_tail`, the DFlash mitigation the KV cache managers already support.

A second effect makes it worse.

items.title: Preserve coroutine runtime errors
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: runs a coroutine synchronously. When an event loop is already running in the calling thread, it executes the coroutine in a helper thread. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

`DynamicInferenceEngine._run_coroutine_sync` runs a coroutine synchronously. When an event loop is already running in the calling thread, it executes the coroutine in a helper thread. The `try` that detects a running loop also wrapped that execution, so a `RuntimeError` raised by the coroutine itself was treated as "no running loop". The bridge then retried on the engine's loop, and the caller saw "This event loop is already running" instead of the real error.

This PR guards only the loop check, so errors raised by the coroutine reach the caller unchanged.

## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

…he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: honor teacher temperature in on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

- DeepScaler

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

items.summary: Base image moved to (v0.24.0). Rebase accordingly: - Drop the partial-wake / dummy-batch hunk — the guard is now upstream in 0.24.0, so patching it is unnecessary and would fail to apply.
items.body:
## Summary

Base image moved to `vllm/vllm-openai:latest-ubuntu2404` (v0.24.0). Rebase `docker/patch/latest/vllm.patch` accordingly:

- **Drop** the `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` partial-wake / dummy-batch hunk — the `if not self.model_executor.is_sleeping` guard is now upstream in 0.24.0, so patching it is unnecessary and would fail to apply.
- **Keep** the `all2all_utils.py` (`max_num_tokens = moe.max_num_tokens`) hunk.
- **Add** `/abort_requests` endpoint (`api_router.py`, from #296) and `GenerateResponse.usage` field (`disagg/protocol.py`, from #303).

items.body:
…efault

- Add torch_memory_saver_hook_mode_preload_cu13.abi3.so to the TMS dynamic library search list. Without this, cu13 (CUDA 13) containers fail to find the preload hook and TMS memory management is disabled.

- Change NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE default from "0" to "1". GB300 (sm103) requires CUMEM for NVLink/NVLS transports; disabling it causes NCCL init failures on Blackwell GPUs.

items.body:
## Summary

`rollout/prefix_cache_hit_rate` (and `avg_cached_tokens_per_sample`) were **structurally 0**. Root cause is three coupled gaps at the vime↔vLLM interface:

1. **vLLM drops `usage` on the non-streaming endpoint.** `/inference/v1/generate`'s `serve_tokens_full_generator` builds a `usage` block (incl. `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, since vime already passes `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`) but hands it to `GenerateResponse(..., usage=usage, ...)` — and `GenerateResponse` (v0.23.0 `serve/disagg/protocol.py`) never declared a `usage` field, so pydantic silently discards it. vim
